meta.name: Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102)
meta.notes: Initial pack: 10 questions across the major AI-102 domains (planning, generative AI, agentic, computer vision, NLP, knowledge mining & document intelligence).

questions.question: You are deploying Azure AI capabilities for an enterprise app and need a single endpoint and key that authorise calls to Vision, Language, Speech and Translator with consolidated billing. Which resource type should you create?
options: A multi-service Azure AI services resource (one shared key)
An Azure AI Foundry hub-only workspace resource by itself
One single-service resource per individual API that you use
An Azure Cognitive Search standard tier search resource only
questions.explanation: A multi-service Azure AI services resource exposes one endpoint and one key that can be used to call all the Azure AI service APIs (Vision, Language, Speech, Translator and more) and consolidates the billing. Single-service resources give per-service endpoints, an AI Foundry hub orchestrates projects rather than serving the inference APIs directly, and AI Search is a retrieval service not an AI API gateway.

questions.question: Your team must rotate the access keys on a production Azure AI Language resource without interrupting client traffic that is already in flight. Which sequence is recommended?
options: Regenerate key1, update all clients to key2, then regenerate key1 again
Regenerate key1, switch all clients to it, and then regenerate key2
Regenerate both keys at the same time and push them to all clients
Disable key auth, recreate the resource and re-deploy each client app
questions.explanation: Azure AI resources expose two keys (key1 and key2) precisely to enable zero-downtime rotation: clients keep using key1 while you regenerate key2 (or vice versa), then you swap clients to the freshly rotated key and rotate the other. Regenerating both at once invalidates live sessions, deleting the resource changes the endpoint, and there is no separate password mechanism.

questions.question: A retailer wants to detect and locate their own product SKUs inside shelf photographs using a small set of labelled images and a no-code training portal. Which Azure service fits best?
options: Azure AI Vision Image Analysis 4.0 with built-in tagging
Azure AI Custom Vision project trained for object detection
Azure AI Video Indexer with a custom-trained person model
Azure AI Document Intelligence custom extraction model
questions.explanation: Azure AI Custom Vision lets you upload labelled images via the portal at customvision.ai and train an image classification or object detection model that returns SKU bounding boxes. Image Analysis returns only generic prebuilt tags, Video Indexer focuses on video and people, and Document Intelligence extracts fields from documents — not retail products.

questions.question: The prebuilt invoice model in Azure AI Document Intelligence is missing several vendor-specific fields that your finance team needs extracted automatically. What should you do next?
options: Train a custom neural extraction model on labelled vendor samples
Upgrade the prebuilt invoice model to its higher pricing tier
Run only Read OCR and parse the raw text with regular expressions
Replace the prebuilt invoice model with the prebuilt receipt model
questions.explanation: When prebuilt models do not cover all required fields, you label a small set of vendor-specific samples and train a custom neural (or template) model in Document Intelligence Studio. There is no higher tier of the prebuilt invoice model that adds fields, regex on raw OCR loses structure and reliability, and the receipt model is for till receipts, not invoices.

questions.question: Your chatbot must classify each user utterance into an intent and extract entities such as dates and locations from it. Which Azure AI Language feature should you use?
options: Conversational language understanding (CLU) trained model
Custom named entity recognition (custom NER) on its own
Sentiment analysis with opinion-mining mode switched on
Language detection combined with key-phrase extraction
questions.explanation: Conversational language understanding (CLU), the successor to LUIS, is purpose-built for intent classification plus entity extraction inside a single model. Custom NER only handles entities, sentiment analysis returns a polarity score, and language detection plus key-phrase extraction does not predict intents at all.

questions.question: A studio wants Azure to speak marketing copy in a voice that matches a specific brand spokesperson, trained from short studio recordings of that person. Which capability is required?
options: Azure Custom Neural Voice (Limited Access programme)
The standard catalogue of prebuilt neural voices only
Speech translation configured with target voice presets
Pronunciation assessment with a speaker profile attached
questions.explanation: Custom Neural Voice trains a synthetic voice from recordings of a real speaker and is gated by Microsoft's Limited Access programme to protect against impersonation. Prebuilt neural voices are generic preset speakers, speech translation translates spoken audio between languages, and pronunciation assessment scores how clearly a learner speaks — none of them produce a custom voice.

questions.question: You want an Azure OpenAI chat deployment to answer questions using your own private PDF policy documents, kept up to date with each release. Which pattern is recommended?
options: Azure AI Search vector index with the On Your Data feature
Fine-tune a GPT model on the PDF text every release cycle
Concatenate all PDF text into the system prompt of each call
Base64-encode the PDFs and inline them in the user prompt
questions.explanation: The recommended Retrieval-Augmented Generation pattern is to chunk and embed the PDFs into an Azure AI Search vector index and let Azure OpenAI's 'on your data' feature retrieve relevant chunks at query time. Fine-tuning is expensive and stale, stuffing all PDFs into the prompt blows past the context window, and Base64-encoded PDFs are not consumable by the chat model.

questions.question: By default, every Azure OpenAI deployment screens prompts and completions for harmful content across categories such as hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content. Which capability provides those built-in filters?
options: Azure AI Content Safety filters built into the deployment
Microsoft Defender for Cloud workload protection rules
Microsoft Purview information protection sensitivity labels
Azure Policy initiatives targeting Generative AI scopes
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI integrates Azure AI Content Safety filters by default, scoring prompts and completions on hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content with severity thresholds and supporting Prompt Shields and protected-material detection. Defender for Cloud handles cloud workload posture, Purview is a data governance product, and Azure Policy enforces resource configuration, not content moderation.

questions.question: Your assistant must call live external APIs (weather, inventory) during a chat turn and weave the results back into its reply. Which Azure OpenAI capability orchestrates that pattern?
options: Function (tool) calling with a tools schema in the request
Fine-tuning the model on transcripts of past API responses
Embedding the API reference documentation into every prompt
Triggering DALL-E image generation after each user turn
questions.explanation: Function (tool) calling lets the model emit a structured JSON call that matches a tools schema you supply; your code executes the real API and feeds the result back in a follow-up turn for the model to summarise. Fine-tuning does not run live APIs, large reference docs in the prompt waste tokens, and DALL-E is an image generator unrelated to tool invocation.

questions.question: You add a 1,536-dimension embedding produced by Azure OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 to each chunk in an Azure AI Search index so it can be retrieved by vector similarity. How should that field be defined?
options: Collection(Edm.Single) with dimensions and a vector search profile
Edm.String marked as both searchable and filterable on writes
Collection(Edm.String) using the standard analyzer on the field
Edm.ComplexType wrapping nested numeric child sub-fields explicitly
questions.explanation: Vector fields in Azure AI Search are typed as Collection(Edm.Single) and carry a `dimensions` value (here 1536) plus a reference to a vector search profile that selects an algorithm such as HNSW. Edm.String is for keyword text, Collection(Edm.String) is for string arrays, and a complex type cannot back vector similarity queries.
